title: script-standards-detail.md tells scripts to pair every ACTION with a log_warn but never says that write_summary promotes every later OK row to WARN once a warning is counted
observation: scripts/aitools-lib.sh write_summary (:860-866 on origin/main 8a9dcb5): 'Auto-promote OK to WARN when warnings have been logged' (`if [ "$cat" = "OK" ] && [ "${WARNINGS:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then cat="WARN"`); scripts/aitools-lib.ps1 Write-Summary (:752-757) the same. reference/script-standards-detail.md 'Severity decision guide' (:239-243): '`log_warn` + `write_summary ACTION` -- user action required; always pair ACTION with a log_warn carrying the same instruction', and 'ACTION items' repeats it; neither section mentions the promotion. scripts/setup-user-config.sh:367-370 works around it by hand: 'It must stay after the config row: write_summary promotes an OK row to WARN once a warning is counted'.
expected: reference/script-standards-detail.md 'End-of-run summary' and 'Severity decision guide' are the specification of row categories; a library behaviour that changes the category a caller passes belongs there. No spec exists for: ordering summary rows around a counted advisory warning.
impact: A script that follows the guide (log_warn + ACTION before its own OK row) reports WARN for a tool that is fine, so the summary panel overstates problems; each script author rediscovers the trap (S3-M3-ConfigKey and its reviewer did on PR #86).
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-ConfigKey-report.md:87 and S3-M3-ConfigKey-Review-pr86-batch4.md:115 (PR #86 batch 4). Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: read scripts/aitools-lib.sh:855-866, scripts/aitools-lib.ps1:752-760, reference/script-standards-detail.md:239-265 ('Severity decision guide', 'Summary coverage rule', 'ACTION items'), scripts/setup-user-config.sh:363-376. Audited #1-#145: #142 (duplicate ERROR rows) is a different summary defect. A draft doc edit exists (S3-M3-Docs approval page row 15, script-standards-detail.md.edit.txt).
suggestedResolution: Option A: document the promotion in 'Severity decision guide' and 'ACTION items' (write the tool's own row before an advisory log_warn + ACTION). Option B: exempt ACTION-paired warnings from promotion in the lib (a counter of advisory warnings, bash and PS1), then document it. The S3-M3-Docs draft takes option A (protected file: approve the draft).

title: No logging contract exists for library-style tools that return their warnings to the caller (the profile resolver), so each caller decides on its own which returned warnings are row-level WARN and which are advisory
observation: scripts/aitools-profile.sh returns diagnostics instead of logging them at level: cmd_user_repo_path prints its warnings as 'warning: ...' lines on stderr and its result on stdout (:770-781 on origin/main 8a9dcb5); it defines log() to stderr before logging_init (:71-79). Callers route them by hand: scripts/setup-user-config.sh derive_warn (:165 onward) sorts each returned warning into 'handled', 'advisory' and 'real' with its own patterns; aitools-lib.sh tool_exception_record logs returned warn lines as detail (:432). reference/logging.md has sections 1-6 (Location, Path separators, Granularity, Rotation, Format, Setup-vs-check) and no section for library-style tools; the script-standards-detail.md exemptions table has no resolver row. Before ConfigKey (PR #86 batch 4) setup-user-config turned every returned warning into a WARN row (S3-M3-Resolver-Review M-finding); that code is fixed, the contract is still unwritten.
expected: No spec exists for: how a tool that returns diagnostics (rather than logging them) reports them, and which returned warnings a caller must count. .claude/rules/script-standards.md 'Error and warning tracking requirement' assumes every script logs and counts its own warnings.
impact: Every new consumer of the resolver (deploy-harness, tool setup scripts in M2) must invent its own warning routing; a wrong choice either downgrades the summary row on every run (the pre-fix setup-user-config behaviour) or hides a real problem at info level.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-Register-keydesign.md:411 (design j finding 1), S3-M3-Resolver-report.md:123 and :125, S3-M3-Resolver-Review-pr86-batch2.md:166. Merged into one entry: the advisory-vs-row-level marker is the same missing contract (its code instance was fixed in setup-user-config.sh:160-185). Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: read scripts/aitools-profile.sh:71-79 and :768-780, scripts/setup-user-config.sh:160-185, grep of reference/logging.md headings and reference/script-standards-detail.md. A draft logging.md section 7 'Library-style tools' exists (S3-M3-Docs approval page row 16).
suggestedResolution: Approve the S3-M3-Docs draft of reference/logging.md section 7 (protected), extended with the advisory/row-level split that setup-user-config.sh derive_warn already implements; add the resolver to the script-standards-detail.md exemptions table. Optional: the resolver tags each warning with its class so callers stop pattern-matching message text.
correctiveAction: Code instance fixed: setup-user-config.sh derive_warn routes advisory warnings to info + one ACTION (PR #86 batch 4).

title: The naming and scope contract for shared-library results (AITLIB_ globals, dot-sourced PowerShell scope, function names a caller also defines) exists only as a code comment in aitools-lib.sh, and the installers already shadow two lib functions
observation: scripts/aitools-lib.sh:125-134 (origin/main 8a9dcb5): 'Result-global contract (PR #80 review3 B1/M1): every result global carries the AITLIB_ prefix and every private helper the _aitlib_ prefix, so they cannot collide with a caller's own variables'. grep -i 'AITLIB|dot-sourc|result global|prefix' over reference/script-standards-detail.md, reference/cross-platform-detail.md and .claude/rules/script-standards.md: no hits. Shadowing: aitools-lib.sh:569 defines relay_child_log and scripts/aitools-install.sh:153 defines its own; aitools-lib.ps1:449 defines Write-JsonlRecord and scripts/aitools-install.ps1:65 defines its own (after dot-sourcing the lib, so the caller's copy wins).
expected: No spec exists for: naming of shared-library result variables, the scope of a dot-sourced PowerShell library, or what a caller's definition of a lib function name means. .claude/rules/script-standards.md 'Required logging helpers' says 'Do not define inline copies' for logging helpers only.
impact: The PR #80 collisions (review3 B1/M1: lib results overwrote callers' USER_REPO_PATH) can recur in any new lib section, since the rule lives where only readers of that block see it; a lib fix to relay_child_log or Write-JsonlRecord silently does not reach the installers that shadow them.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-LibFix-report.md:129 (repeating the Review3 marker on PR #80) and S3-M3-LibKey-report.md:95. Merged: same missing contract. Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: read scripts/aitools-lib.sh:120-150, grep for relay_child_log / Write-JsonlRecord / jsonl_record definitions in the lib and installers, grep of the three spec files. The Review3 full report is not in the repo (PR #82 points to it); its other markers are unknown.
suggestedResolution: Add a 'Library contract' paragraph to reference/script-standards-detail.md 'Shared library' (protected): AITLIB_/_aitlib_ and $script:AitLib* prefixes, assignment only inside functions, callers copy results right after the call, and callers never redefine a lib function (or must name the override, as entry-point logging does). Then remove or rename the installers' relay_child_log / Write-JsonlRecord copies, or record them as deliberate overrides.

title: The two JSON engines write the same number differently (aitools-json.pl keeps the source text such as 0.10; aitools-json.ps1 writes 0.1), so bash and PowerShell writers of one shared file produce different bytes
observation: scripts/aitools-json.pl:68-70 (origin/main 8a9dcb5): 'Numbers keep their source lexeme byte for byte' (`sub numnorm { return $_[0] }`). scripts/aitools-json.ps1 ConvertTo-JText (:66-70) formats doubles and decimals with `[System.Convert]::ToString($v, [System.Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture)`, which writes 0.10 as 0.1. The S3-M3-JsonRename reviewer verified the difference with a round trip on the base aitools-json.ps1 (PR #86 comment); not re-run here.
expected: .claude/rules/cross-platform.md 'Platform targeting principle' (paired scripts behave the same); the resolver and profile.json are written by both engines (commander decision: dotprofile writes auto-commit and push, N-Q2).
impact: A profile.json value with trailing zeros changes bytes when a Windows machine rewrites it, so the dotprofile gets diff-only commits that flip between machines; byte-level comparisons between bash and PS1 test outputs fail.
discoveryContext: Marker in S3-M3-JsonRename-report.md:69 (from its reviewer, PR #86 re-key batch 1). Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5 by reading scripts/aitools-json.pl:60-72 and scripts/aitools-json.ps1:60-90; no round trip run. Audited #1-#145: no match.
suggestedResolution: Keep the source lexeme in the PS1 engine too (parse numbers into a wrapper that carries the original text, as perl does), and add a parity case with 0.10 and a 17-digit value to tests/profile/test-profile.sh for both engines.

title: No rule says each pushed batch of a stacked PR keeps CI green or declares a deliberately red CI, so a batch landed with macOS and Linux CI red and an ordinary commit message
observation: Commit b70fc64 'Key machine profiles by machine id in the native resolver (re-key batch 2)' (2026-10-22) was pushed to the stacked re-key PR #86 with the macos and linux CI jobs red, and its message did not mention a CI failure (S3-M3-Resolver-Review-pr86-batch2.md finding M1, marker :165). grep -i 'CI green|keeps CI|red CI' over .claude, reference and shared: no hits.
expected: No spec exists for: CI status of intermediate pushed batches on a stacked PR. Nearest: /delegate D-DEL4 shipping terms (run the repo's checks before push) and #144 (merge gating on review verdicts).
impact: A red batch in a stack hides whether later batches broke CI or inherited the failure, and reviewers of the next batch start from an unknown baseline; reviewers and the commander learn it only from the CI page.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-Resolver-Review-pr86-batch2.md:165 and S3-M3-Resolver-report.md:124. Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified: `git log -1 b70fc64`, grep of .claude, reference and shared. The CI run state itself was not re-checked (from the reviewer).
frameworks: Trunk-based development 'keep the build green': every pushed change passes CI, or the push says why not (a declared, tracked red build).
suggestedResolution: Add to /delegate D-DEL4 shipping terms and reference/pre-push-checklist.md: each pushed batch keeps CI green; a deliberately red batch says so in its commit message and PR body with the reason and the batch that turns it green. Optional detection: reviewers check `gh pr checks` per batch.

title: The lib's resolver runner trusts an exit code only with a 'via' result line, which register and migrate never print, and the output-validation rule it implements is written nowhere outside the lib
observation: scripts/aitools-lib.sh _aitlib_profile_run (:154-159, :216-225 on origin/main 8a9dcb5): 'every resolver command prints a "via" line on 0 (found) and 1 (none). Exit 0 or 1 without one ... is rewritten to 2'. scripts/aitools-profile.sh emits `put via` only in user-repo-path (:783), resolve (:872), exception-get (:907), exception-set (:1040) and the profile command (:1147); cmd_register (:1219) and cmd_migrate (:1443) print none. scripts/aitools:196-201 therefore keeps its own runner: 'Not the lib runner ... register and migrate print no "via" line'. No lib wrapper calls register or migrate today (grep 'register|migrate' in scripts/aitools-lib.sh: comments only, :138, :319, :367), so the mismatch is latent. reference/script-standards-detail.md 'External command error handling' says nothing about validating a child's output before trusting its exit code; the resolver's 'not found' exit 1 equals a set -e death and pwsh's own failure code (S3-M3-LibFix-Review M1).
expected: The lib's own header contract (aitools-lib.sh:154) claims every resolver command prints a via line; .claude/rules/script-standards.md 'External command error handling' (check exit codes, distinguish failure modes). No spec exists for: validating a child tool's result lines before trusting its exit code.
impact: The first lib wrapper for register or migrate (deploy-harness or M2 tool scripts) reports every successful registration as a resolver error; meanwhile user init carries a second runner that can drift from the lib's.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-UserInit-report.md:96 (owner: lib) and S3-M3-LibFix-Review-pr80.md:199 (no rule). Merged: the rule the lib implements and the case where it misfires. Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: read scripts/aitools-lib.sh:136-225, grep `put via` in scripts/aitools-profile.sh, scripts/aitools:196-205. Parallel mission S3-MF-Adopt owns scripts/aitools-lib.* now; this entry does not assume its outcome.
suggestedResolution: Accept a `result` line as well as `via` in _aitlib_profile_run / Invoke-AitLibProfile (the UserInit report's fix), then let user init use the lib runner. Document the rule in reference/script-standards-detail.md 'External command error handling' (protected): a wrapper trusts a child's exit code only together with the child's result lines, and a child whose failure codes collide with shell/runtime codes must print result lines.

title: The isolated-HOME rule for test and probe runs does not cover the working directory, so a relative path from a fixture's config.json wrote into the main checkout
observation: S3-M3-UserInit-Review-pr86-batch5.md:125: 'A relative path in a fixture's config.json (or any relative path a script takes from config) writes into the agent's cwd, here the main checkout. Probe and test scripts should cd into scratch first.' The mission packet section 5 says 'isolated HOME under your worktree scratch (#86)'; shared/skills/delegate/SKILL.md (origin/main 8a9dcb5) mentions isolated HOME at :184 and :212-213 and has no cwd or working-directory instruction (grep -i 'cwd|working directory': no hits). The relative-repos-path regression itself was fixed in PR #89.
expected: Mission packet section 5 and incident #86/#140: test and probe runs must not touch the real user state or the main checkout. No spec exists for: the working directory of isolated test runs.
impact: A delegate following the isolated-HOME rule exactly can still write fixture output into the main checkout (or any directory it was launched from), where it is mistaken for real work, harvested, or committed by another agent.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-UserInit-report.md:98 and S3-M3-UserInit-Review-pr86-batch5.md:125. Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Related #140 (worktree isolation refuses HOME overrides), #86.
suggestedResolution: Add one line to /delegate 'Environment limits' and the dotprofile delegation.md (protected): isolated runs set HOME and cd into the scratch directory first (or pass absolute paths only), and probes check that no file appeared outside scratch (`git status` of the launch directory before/after).

title: cross-platform-detail.md omits three traps that broke M3 code or tests: PowerShell variable names ignore case, success-stream output from in-process child scripts becomes a function's return value, and .ps1 files are checked out with CRLF
observation: (1) S3-M3-Resolver-report.md:126: '`foreach ($e in $E)` silently overwrote the collection in Invoke-Migrate (found by the parity tests, fixed)'. (2) S3-M3-UserInit-Review-pr86-batch5.md:126 (m1): a PowerShell function that returns an exit code and runs a child script in-process without discarding its output stream returns that output, so `exit (Fn)` exits 0. (3) .gitattributes:2 `*.ps1 text eol=crlf`; tests/profile/test-user-init.sh:328-329 adds `\r?` before `$` because line-anchored perl patterns miss CRLF lines. reference/cross-platform-detail.md (origin/main 8a9dcb5) has sections for pipeline encoding, clipboard, working directory, Refresh-Path, Git Bash PATH shadowing and Strawberry Perl text mode, and none for these three.
expected: .claude/rules/cross-platform.md 'Windows platform gotchas' points to reference/cross-platform-detail.md for platform traps. No spec exists for: these three.
impact: Each trap fails silently (a clobbered variable, a wrong exit code, a test that matches nothing and passes); the next PowerShell or test author rediscovers them.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-Resolver-report.md:126, S3-M3-UserInit-report.md:99 and :100, S3-M3-UserInit-Review-pr86-batch5.md:126. Merged: all three are missing gotcha entries in the same file with the same fix. Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: cat .gitattributes, read tests/profile/test-user-init.sh:325-337, grep of reference/cross-platform-detail.md headings. Traps (1) and (2) are cited from the reports (code instances fixed), not reproduced.
suggestedResolution: Add three short gotcha sections to reference/cross-platform-detail.md and one-line pointers in .claude/rules/cross-platform.md 'Windows platform gotchas' (protected): distinct variable names that differ by more than case; `$null = & child.ps1` or `| Out-Null` inside functions whose return value is used; `\r?$` (or strip CR) in line-anchored patterns over .ps1 files.
correctiveAction: Instances fixed in PR #86 (Invoke-Migrate variable rename; user init output handling; test-user-init.sh CRLF-tolerant patterns).

title: profile.json scaffolded by the resolver (register --create, user init on a dotprofile without one) carries only meta.schemaRevision, no meta.intent

title: When profile.json already had uncommitted changes, tool_exception_record tells the user to 'run git push' although the resolver committed nothing
observation: scripts/aitools-profile.sh commit_profile (:960-970 on origin/main 8a9dcb5): with profile.json dirty before the write, exception-set writes the file but does not commit it and warns 'profile.json had uncommitted changes before this write -- not committed automatically; review and commit profile.json in $dir by hand'. scripts/aitools-lib.sh tool_exception_record (:439-447) picks the first warn line matching /commit|push|git repository/, logs 'tool exception for $slug saved but not pushed (...)' and adds ACTION 'run git push in <dotprofile>'; scripts/aitools-lib.ps1 (:371-376) does the same.
expected: reference/script-standards-detail.md 'Severity decision guide' (an ACTION is the instruction the user must follow); the resolver's own warning says to review and commit by hand.
impact: The user runs `git push` as told, pushes nothing (or pushes unrelated commits), and the tool exception stays uncommitted on this machine only, so the other machines never see the decision.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-Docs-Check-findings.md:160 and S3-M3-Docs-approval-page.md:103 (finding F18). Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: read scripts/aitools-lib.sh:405-478, scripts/aitools-lib.ps1:360-380, scripts/aitools-profile.sh:947-972. The marker's second half (wrapper headers describe exit 3 as 'matched by hostname only or not at all') was not verified against the resolver's refusal cases and is not part of this entry. Parallel mission S3-MF-Adopt owns scripts/aitools-lib.* now.
suggestedResolution: Have the resolver return a 'committed' tag (true/false) next to 'pushed'; the wrappers then give ACTION 'review and commit profile.json in <dir>, then git push' when nothing was committed, and 'run git push in <dir>' only after a commit. Bash and PS1 together, with a dirty-profile test case.

title: logging_init can print a console warning on stdout before a script can redirect its logging, so every script whose stdout carries data must redefine log() before calling it
observation: scripts/aitools-lib.sh logging_init (:658-666 on origin/main 8a9dcb5) calls _log_aitools_environment, which logs a warn when an AITOOLS_ENVIRONMENT override is invalid (:671-676, log_warn at :674); log() writes console lines with printf to stdout (:681-691). scripts/aitools-profile.sh, whose stdout is its result, works around it by defining log() to stderr before logging_init (:71-79: 'Defined before logging_init, whose environment check may already log a warning'). The lib has no option to send console logging to stderr. The S3-Profile reviewer reported the same for aitools-lib.ps1 Initialize-Logging (PR #73); the PS1 side was not re-read here.
expected: .claude/rules/script-standards.md 'Log line format' (structured console lines) and the resolver's result-on-stdout contract; no spec exists for: console logging of scripts whose stdout is data.
impact: A data-returning script that forgets the workaround emits a log line in its result stream whenever the environment override is wrong, which its caller parses as data (wrong path, wrong alias) or rejects.
discoveryContext: Marker in S3-Profile-Review-pr73.md:96 (and the PR #73 review comment). Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: read scripts/aitools-lib.sh:650-700, scripts/aitools-profile.sh:65-80. Parallel mission S3-MF-Adopt owns scripts/aitools-lib.* now.
suggestedResolution: Add a lib switch honoured by log()/Log (for example LOG_CONSOLE_FD=2 / $script:LogConsoleToStderr) that a script sets before logging_init; replace the resolver's local log() override with it.

title: cross-platform.md does not say whether a bash library calling its PowerShell counterpart (aitools-lib.sh running aitools-profile.ps1 under Git Bash) needs cross-language approval or the OS-dispatch form

discoveryContext: Marker in S3-M3-LibFix-Review-pr80.md:189. Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22.
